name: ncdc
why: A terminal Direct Connect client opens a door into the old DC++ peer-to-peer protocol nobody uses anymore.

brief.what_it_is: ncdc is a terminal client for Direct Connect, a peer-to-peer file-sharing network, with an ncurses interface. It connects to multiple hubs at once over both the ADC and NMDC protocols, handles chat and private messages, browses hub user lists and remote file lists, and manages shares, searches, uploads, downloads and queues. It is written in C and released under the MIT license.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes ncdc as a lightweight direct connect client with a friendly ncurses interface. It is aimed at people who want a full-featured DC client that runs in a terminal.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage and install page do not explain the internals beyond the feature list. The feature list includes TTH-checked, multi-source, segmented downloads, TLS-secured hub and client connections, encrypted ADC SUDP UDP messages, sendfile() for uploads, and file-list opening in a background thread.

brief.install_notes: Required libraries: ncurses, zlib, bzip2, sqlite3, glib2 and gnutls. Generic source build is ./configure, make, then make install as root. Static Linux binaries for x86-64, i486, ARM and AArch64 are linked against musl and bundle their dependencies; extract the tarball and run ./ncdc. There is an Android installer for Android 2.3 and later that uses the static binary. Packages exist for Arch (AUR), Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, FreeBSD, Frugalware, GNU Guix, Gentoo, Homebrew, OpenSUSE, Source Mage and Void. The install page warns that the system-specific instructions have not been tested in a long time. The OpenIndiana and OpenBSD sections need extra configure flags. The Cygwin section needs a list of Cygwin packages and runs under Cygwin. No account or hardware is needed. The page does not describe first-run configuration beyond the homepage's hub-connection features.
brief.standout: It is a full-featured terminal client for Direct Connect, covering both ADC and NMDC, with features the homepage calls uncommon in other DC clients: per-hub connection settings, a single listen port for TLS and TCP, Trust on First Use for TLS hubs, subdirectory refreshing, and nick highlighting in chat. The author says it is written in C with relatively low memory use.
brief.status: Passive maintenance, according to the homepage: 'No active development has been happening for a while, but I'm still around to implement fixes and the occasional feature update.' The latest version is 1.25, dated 2025-03-04. The homepage also says that 'given development is currently kind of dead, there's a good chance none of it will happen anytime soon.' No commit dates were checked.
brief.caveats: The author has not actively developed it for a while, so new features are unlikely. Several system-specific install instructions are marked as possibly broken. Building from source does not always work, according to the install page. The homepage lists missing features: NAT traversal, OP features, and SOCKS support. Requires a C toolchain and several libraries for source builds. Windows support is only through Cygwin. The static binaries target Linux only; other platforms need a request to the author.

judge.reason: A terminal client for both ADC and NMDC offers a hands-on window into an unusual, still-running peer-to-peer network and its hub protocols.

entry.title: ncdc
entry.tldr: A terminal client for Direct Connect, the hub-based peer-to-peer file-sharing network, speaking both the ADC and NMDC protocols through an ncurses interface.
entry.deeper_look:
ncdc connects to several Direct Connect hubs at once. It handles hub chat and private messages, browses user lists and other users' file lists, and manages your own shares, searches, uploads, downloads and queue. It is written in C and released under the MIT license.

Direct Connect is an older style of peer-to-peer network. Instead of one global swarm, you join a hub, a server run by a community, and see the people and shares there. Clients then transfer files directly between each other. ncdc speaks both of the protocols in use: the older NMDC and the newer ADC.

The feature list shows some of the protocol machinery: downloads checked against TTH hashes, multi-source and segmented transfers, TLS on hub and client connections, encrypted ADC SUDP search replies over UDP, and sendfile() for uploads. Reading how a client handles these is a way into how a hub-based network differs from the swarm model most people know.

The homepage calls it "a lightweight direct connect client with a friendly ncurses interface." It is in passive maintenance: version 1.25 is dated 2025-03-04, and the author says new features are unlikely.
entry.install:
brew install ncdc
# No account or hardware needed. You will need the address of a Direct Connect hub to join.

Starts the ncurses interface, where you can configure your nick and shares and connect to a hub.

entry.whats_unique: It is a full terminal client for both ADC and NMDC. The homepage lists per-hub settings, one listen port for TLS and TCP, and Trust on First Use for TLS hubs as uncommon among DC clients.
entry.caveats: Development is passive and new features are unlikely, and the homepage lists NAT traversal, OP features and SOCKS support as missing.
